title: Turn Any Book Into an AI Skill You'll Actually Use
author: Vicky Zhao
summary: Argues that the usual way people turn a book into an AI skill fails because of compounding abstraction: the author already abstracted experience into a book, a summary strips the nuance and examples, and asking an LLM to distil that into a skill is an abstraction of an abstraction of an abstraction — which is why the resulting skill is vague and average. Feed the AI rich context instead of compressed summaries, since AI is good at digesting volume. A skill only earns its place if it does three things: knows when to invoke the method, drives an actual behaviour change, and records and reviews what happened — closing a feedback loop, which AI is unusually good at maintaining because it tracks and surfaces over time. Frames mastery through shu-ha-ri, the Japanese martial arts and tea ceremony progression. Learning has not occurred until behaviour changes; anything short of that is intellectual fantasising.
